statement.p: Suppose that a person is taking a walk along a long straight path and walks at a constant rate of 3 miles per hour. Below is a graph of the velocity function v(t)=3, where time t is in hours.

image.shortdescription: Graph of a horizontal line at height 3 over time 0 to 5.

description.p: Graph of v(t)=3 for t>0 in the coordinate plane with horizontal axis time (hours) and vertical axis velocity (mph).

statement.p: How far did the person travel in the first 2 hours?

This distance is the area under the velocity graph and above the x-axis between
x=0 and x=1
x=0 and x=2
x=1 and x=2
Find an algebraic formula s(t) for the position of the person at time t, assuming that s(0)=0.

Note that because the velocity graph is above the x-axis, we know that the position function s is
Decreasing
Increasing
Sometimes increasing and sometimes decreasing
Can't tell
